# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 21:58 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 247 active entries of tips_notebook.json (46 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so state your vote before each nomination and trial, then vote that way. If you switch, say why before the vote, because announced totals expose hidden mismatches. (seen in 30 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one mechanical case: an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a broken claim, group elimination, or a lone visitor to a Katana victim. First ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester or Executioner). (seen in 32 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But a corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim, with no harmless explanation, is near-proof; don't let caveats acquit them. (seen in 29 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction. Actions are optional, roles can repeat, and a role-block explains any missing result. 'Roles can repeat' only means a claim isn't disproved; it is not support for it. (seen in 28 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, but post results publicly by day. Deaths reveal no role, and the result of the night you die never reaches your will. (seen in 27 games)
- Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. Repeated evasion becomes its own case. (seen in 7 games)
- Budget is limited: ask a concrete question once, by name, and save budget for trials and the late rounds. (seen in 8 games)

## Village
- Post your role, night, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. If someone copies your claim, counterclaim at once with your full log. (seen in 16 games)
- Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM: it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 20 games)
- Stay quiet about power roles on Day 1. Don't be the loudest organizer, who is a common first Katana target. (seen in 24 games)
- Once a player is shown to be Yakuza by a mechanical result, suspect those who pushed No or delay at the nomination, or defended them. Compare stated votes with the totals to find hidden votes. (seen in 27 games)
- A PM link is a lead, never a hang on its own. Jesters and Executioners leave PM trails on purpose. (seen in 28 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises, such as a slip naming a Yakuza-only role, far above awkward wording. (seen in 20 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool all game. Read every cause of death, press anyone who admits an action without naming it, and expect a multi-death ignite night. (seen in 17 games)
- Surviving a Katana attack proves nothing without a credible Medic: Neutrals have innate Defense. 'I was blocked' is unverifiable, but it fully explains a missing result. (seen in 15 games)
- Leave a likely Jester alive. If you must hang one, agree publicly on a bare Guilty majority, with confirmed power roles voting Innocent, since revenge Divine-attacks a random Guilty voter. (seen in 15 games)
- An archive is a sample, not a census. Use slot math to choose whom to press, audit or watch, then hang on the contradiction that test produces. (seen in 14 games)

## Yakuza
- Don't defend a doomed teammate unless the team's votes can actually save them; do that math in night chat. On a likely-Jester nominee, some of you should vote Innocent to stay out of the revenge draw. (seen in 34 games)
- Never put plans in daytime PMs. Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and the town treats a visible teammate PM cluster as a lead. (seen in 30 games)
- Fake claims must survive the real holder's counterclaim, token audits, exact-role checks and visit logs. Never claim a Yakuza-only role, even as a hedge. (seen in 18 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night: with two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 21 games)
- After a failed attack, remove or block the protector instead of retrying. Kill Fortune Tellers and other info roles before their results build a shortlist. (seen in 19 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit someone could have seen. Agree a cover action in night chat and admit the visit at once with it. (seen in 15 games)
- Use rig, puppet and other one-shot tokens early. Never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee. (seen in 18 games)
- Never speak from night-chat knowledge, e.g. who held the Katana or who was blocked. Village: demand the source of any such slip immediately. (seen in 7 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked. If you must explain it, pick one claim at once and never switch under pressure. (seen in 6 games)

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so say so when you post a Not Evil result. (seen in 16 games)

## Fortune Teller
- Post both raw totals labeled by night every Day from Day 2, kept separate from your deductions. A visitor total of 1 on a Katana night makes the lone visitor the holder. (seen in 8 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana: use it nightly on claimed investigators, rotating so a Pharmacist can't predict you. Spend a token on self-protection the night you claim. (seen in 21 games)

## Vigilante
- Dying with unused tokens is the usual failure. Set a trigger by Day 2-3, fire a 1-token Basic shot on a solid lead, and post it if the shot fails against innate Defense. (seen in 11 games)

## Clerk
- Rig a Day when a Village player can win a nomination but not a Guilty majority, and decide the night you can use it. Clerks who hold the token usually die with it. (seen in 18 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused, or 2 if anyone questions you. Douse players unlikely to be hanged soon. (seen in 12 games)

lessons.tip: Vary your investigation targets and post each result with the night number immediately; a Sheriff who repeatedly checks the same Not Evil players gives Yakuza a free read, and a Not Evil result on a Katana holder is only meaningful if you cross-check it against visit logs.

Trust exact-role checks (Coroner examines of the dead, Oracle guesses that hit, Vigilante kills) over random Seer pairs. The Village hanged three players on pairs and visit-group readings while the Coroner's confirmed reads were the only solid evidence, and the Cartographer's group lists changed several times.

Do not PM a teammate in daytime, even about something harmless. The Day 3 PM from Alice to me became the lead that drove the Day 4 nomination and the later votes. Any visible PM cluster is read as a link, so keep coordination to night chat.

tips_feedback.tip: Never flatly deny a visit someone could have seen. Agree a cover action in night chat and admit the visit at once with it.
tips_feedback.why: I denied the Night 2 Katana visit outright, and the group-size logs made that denial the central case against me. Agreeing a cover action in night chat beforehand would have let me admit a harmless visit instead.

tips_feedback.tip: Never put plans in daytime PMs. Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and the town treats a visible teammate PM cluster as a lead.
tips_feedback.why: Our night-chat coordination stayed hidden, so the Village never got plan contents. But the one Day 3 PM from Alice to me still became the lead, so the tip was right but the PM itself was a hurt.

tips_feedback.tip: Use rig, puppet and other one-shot tokens early. Never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee.
tips_feedback.why: I held both swap tokens all game and spent none, so they were never used to protect the Katana or redirect a Seer or Medic result. The tip is right that one-shot tokens are worth more used early.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a player is shown to be Yakuza by a mechanical result, suspect those who pushed No or delay at the nomination, or defended them.
tips_feedback.why: Other Village players applied this to Alice and Frank after Ivan's Coroner reads, and it drove a fast hanging chain. For the Yakuza side, it meant that a single confirmed Yakuza read sent the Village after the people defending that player.

lessons.tip: Vary your protection targets and self-protect (1 token for Standard) on nights when your claim is public and a Standard Katana is plausible. Protecting the same claimed Seer on three nights made your pattern easy to read, and I never self-protected even when I was the likely target.
Attacks kill only if strictly higher than Defense, so Standard protection fully stops a Standard Katana. Count that when deciding whether a victim was protected or whether the attacker was Strong.
Post your group sizes with names, once, and keep them fixed. Shifting lists made the Heidi visitor question unusable and gave Yakuza a way to muddy the Village's main lead.
Use examines on dead or executed players to test claims that cannot be checked any other way. The Alice and Frank examines were the decisive Yakuza confirmations this game, so plan them early.
Do not vote Guilty on a single random Seer pair. My Day 4 Guilty vote on Alice rested on one pair, and I should have asked for a second independent check first.

tips_feedback.tip: Free Standard protection stops the Katana: use it nightly on claimed investigators, rotating so a Pharmacist can't predict you.
tips_feedback.why: Protecting Niaj on Night 4 made the Katana attack fail, which confirmed the Seer and my Medic claim. I did not rotate enough, though, since Niaj was my target on three of five nights.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend a token on self-protection the night you claim.
tips_feedback.why: I never followed it, and a 1-token Standard self-protection on Night 5 would have blocked the Katana that killed me. The tip was right, and I ignored it.

lessons.tip: Spend a chosen-pair token on one suspect paired with a player already confirmed Good by an exact-role check or a Sheriff read. A same or different result on two unknowns, like my Night 5 Erin and Judy pair, only shows they match and resolves nothing.
A random Seer pair is a lead, not a case. Before hanging on one, require a second check: a Coroner exact role, a visit log, or a Sheriff result on the same player.
Ask each denier for one plain yes or no early and pin it publicly. A Katana holder must have visited the victim, so one flat no-visit denial was provably false, but the table never pinned it down.
Post each night's Seer result at the first Day it is due. My late posting of Night 2 and Night 3 results let the Yakuza frame my reports as unverified.
Never flatly deny a visit that the holder's own role or the Katana rules force. Agree a cover action in night chat and admit it early, because a lone checkable denial becomes the case against you.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one mechanical case.
tips_feedback.why: My Guilty votes on Alice and Frank each rested on a named chain (Ivan's Coroner read plus Niaj's pair), and both were Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action; a corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim is near-proof.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi's 2-group partner analysis narrowed the Night 2 holder to Erin or Judy, and Judy was the holder.

tips_feedback.tip: Free Standard protection stops the Katana: use it nightly on claimed investigators.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory's Night 4 protection on me stopped a Standard Katana, which supported the Medic claim and kept me alive.

summary:
The Village won 9-3 without losing a player to a mis-hang. Every Yakuza was hanged on a chain of mechanical results.

The decisive information came from three sources:
- **Dave's Night 2 Cartographer sizes (3,2,2,1...).** Once Bob's, Mallory's and Grace's visits were placed, Heidi's killer had to be her lone 2-group partner.
- **Niaj's Seer pairs.** Alice and Frank matched on Night 2, and Carol and Alice differed on Night 3. Carol was anchored as Good by Bob's Sheriff read and by her correct Oracle guesses.
- **Ivan's Coroner exams.** These confirmed Alice as Puppeteer and Frank as Ritualist after each was hanged.

Mallory's free Standard protection on the confirmed Seer stopped the Night 4 Katana, which bought a full extra cycle.

The Yakuza lost mainly through passivity and avoidable tells:
- They ended the game with every token unspent: the puppet token, both swap tokens and both ritual tokens. Frank even declined a near-certain Divine Ritualist guess of Seer on Niaj, who had been publicly confirmed.
- Judy held the Katana all game and flatly denied visiting Heidi, while a Cartographer had already isolated Heidi's partner.
- Alice sent Judy a visible Day 3 PM that was later cited against both of them.
- Frank and Judy voted No/Innocent on each doomed teammate; the hidden vote logs show those Yakuza No votes making up the full No column on both Alice's and Frank's nominations.

Village mistakes:
- Dave fumbled his group arithmetic several times, which let the Yakuza attack his credibility.
- Mallory never used her tokens to protect herself and died with 2 left.
- Niaj misread his Night 5 Erin/Judy 'same' result as 'both Yakuza', when it actually reflected Judy holding the Katana and reading Good. Erin's elimination reasoning was the correct reading.

lessons.tip: When a Cartographer, Scout or Fortune Teller is publicly claimed, assume the Katana visit will be isolated in the visit graph. Before the kill, either move the Katana to a member with a believable visiting cover claim, or use a Smuggler swap or Pharmacist block to blur the graph. Never claim Vanilla and flatly deny a visit that the group sizes can pin on you.
lessons.evidence: Judy held the Katana every night and kept claiming Vanilla with no visits. Dave's N2 sizes left Heidi in a 2-group with one partner. By Day 6 elimination left only 'Erin or Judy', and Judy's repeated denials became the case that hanged her. Her 2 swap tokens were never used.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza (Ritualist, Puppeteer and other token roles)
lessons.tip: Spend one-shot tokens when the payoff is near-certain. A role publicly confirmed by an Oracle is a free Ritualist target, and a Divine guess beats any Medic. Holding tokens 'for later' usually means dying with them.
lessons.evidence: Carol publicly confirmed Niaj as Seer on Day 3. On N4, Frank proposed a Divine ritual on Niaj but backed down over fear of exposure. The Standard Katana was then stopped by Mallory's protection. Frank was hanged the next day with both tokens unused, and Alice never used her puppet.

lessons.tip: Don't vote as a bloc to save a teammate who is clearly doomed. Hidden No/Innocent counts that match your team size, and a public Innocent with no stated check, become the next case. Consider bussing so you survive longer.
lessons.evidence: Alice's nomination passed 7-3 and her trial ended 7-3, with Frank and Judy the hidden No/Innocent votes. Judy publicly announced Innocent on Frank with no check; Grace, Ivan and Mallory cited that flip on Day 5-6, and Grace and Ivan named it in the case that hanged her.

lessons.tip: Chain alignment results through anchored players. A Seer pair becomes a mechanical case once one member is independently confirmed Good, and an exact-role check on the hanged player then extends the chain to their pair partners.
lessons.evidence: Carol was anchored by Bob's Not Evil read and two correct Oracle hits. So Niaj's N3 'Carol/Alice different' hanged Alice. Ivan's exam of Alice (Puppeteer) plus Niaj's N2 'Alice/Frank same' hanged Frank. Ivan then confirmed Frank as Ritualist.

lessons.tip: A lone surviving Yakuza holding the Katana reads Good to every alignment check, every night. A 'same' result pairing a Good player with the suspected holder proves nothing. Rely on visit elimination instead, and don't spend a Seer token on a pair that includes the likely holder.
lessons.evidence: On N5 Niaj spent his only token on Erin/Judy and got 'same', then wrongly concluded 'both are Yakuza'. Bob's N4 check also read Judy as Not Evil. Erin's elimination argument was the correct reading.

lessons.tip: Before posting a deduction from group sizes, place every claimed visit first. Post sizes once, clearly labeled by night, and never revise the list in public. Repeated corrections hand the Yakuza a 'his lists keep changing' defense. Also write your planned map target in your will.
lessons.evidence: Dave first said Heidi was in the 3-group and left himself off his own candidate list, then corrected himself several times. Judy, Frank and Alice used 'Dave's lists changed four times' as their main defense through Day 6. Dave mapped Judy on N3, which named her group, but he died and the result never reached his will.

lessons.tip: Keep giving free Standard protection to the confirmed top information role. But once you are confirmed and the Katana has already failed against your target, expect to be the next target, and spend tokens on Strong self-protection rather than dying with them.
lessons.evidence: Mallory protected Niaj on N4 and stopped the Katana. On N5 she protected Niaj again, and Judy switched targets and killed Mallory, who still had 2 unused medic tokens.

lessons.tip: Keep all coordination in night chat. A visible daytime PM between two players who later turn out to be Yakuza ties them together, whatever its contents.
lessons.evidence: Alice's Day 3 PM to Judy ('say nothing new until Ivan's result') was publicly noted. After Ivan exposed Alice as Puppeteer, that PM was cited against Judy in her Day 6 trial.

issues.description: In post-game feedback Mallory (Medic) said the token-cost line in her prompt seemed to contradict the rules, under which Standard protection is free and a token buys Strong. She had to infer that free Standard protection was allowed. The role prompt or summary for the Medic may misstate token costs.

The Surveyor result text ('One of them, chosen at random, has the role Sheriff') was flagged by Grace as ambiguous about whether other group members could share the role. Grace then told the table 'exactly one of them is Sheriff/Oracle/Medic', which the result does not show. Clearer wording would prevent this misreading.

On Night 4 the Yakuza (Frank and Judy) turned down a Divine Ritualist guess on Niaj. Frank said a correct guess 'tells the victim I'm the Ritualist', and Judy said a Ritualist death 'exposes Frank'. Under R3/R12 a successful Ritualist kill reveals only the cause of death, not who the Ritualist is. Only a wrong guess publicly names the Ritualist. They misunderstood which outcome exposes the player.

On Day 3 Dave (Cartographer) wrongly said Heidi's Katana visit would be in the 3-group. He then gave several conflicting candidate lists, some leaving himself out and some including Frank. Other players treated the size-only output as if it named group members. Many later arguments said things like 'Dave's N2 sizes put Frank in a singleton', but sizes alone can't place a specific player. The Cartographer output (sizes only, no names without a map) confused several players.

An API retry error (HTTP 429 from OpenRouter, model anthropic/claude-opus-5.5) appeared in the game log during Night 5. It was retried and resolution went on correctly. It is a transient infrastructure error, not a game-logic problem.
